title: Repairs and Maintenance Policy
author: P008
summary: Sets out Silvering's repair responsibilities, the four repair priorities and target times, appointments, access, recharges and how residents can report a repair.

version_history.change: Full rewrite after move to in-house repairs service
Aligned with Awaab's Law (in force 27 Oct 2025); damp and mould now cross-refers to Damp & Mould Policy; routine target changed from 20 working days to 28 calendar days
Recharge tariff updated for 2026/27; MySilvering photo upload added; no-access process clarified

blocks.p: This policy explains how {{company.fictional_name}} keeps its homes safe, in good repair and compliant with the law. It applies to all rented homes (social rent, affordable rent, older persons and supported, and market rent) and to the communal areas of blocks where we are the freeholder. Shared owners and leaseholders are responsible for repairs inside their own homes; their lease sets out what we repair in the building structure and communal areas.

Repairs are delivered mainly by our in-house team of multi-trade operatives based at the Aylesford depot and scheduled through FieldLoop. Specialist work (drainage, roofing, some electrical work and gas servicing overflow) is carried out by approved subcontractors under the Subcontractor Management Procedure.

bullets: Landlord and Tenant Act 1985, section 11 (structure, exterior and installations for water, gas, electricity, sanitation and heating)
Homes (Fitness for Human Habitation) Act 2018
Housing Act 2004 and the Housing Health and Safety Rating System (HHSRS)
Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2025 - Awaab's Law, in force from 27 October 2025
Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 and the Electrical Safety Standards that apply to social landlords
The Regulator of Social Housing's Safety and Quality Standard, and the Decent Homes Standard
The Housing Ombudsman's Complaint Handling Code

rows: Structure, roof, walls, windows, external doors
Replacing glass broken by the resident or their visitors
Heating, hot water, boilers, storage heaters
Yes, including annual gas safety check
Bleeding radiators, topping up boiler pressure
Light bulbs, plugs and fuses in appliances
Door handles, damage, replacing for decoration
Investigating causes and fixing them (see Damp & Mould Policy)
Reporting promptly, using extractor fans, not blocking vents
table.caption: Table 1 - Summary of repair responsibilities (full list in the Resident Handbook)

blocks.p: Every repair is given a priority when it is reported. The contact centre adviser or repairs planner uses the FieldLoop question set to decide the priority. If in doubt, the higher priority is used. Target times run from the moment the repair is reported, not from when it is logged.

rows: An immediate risk to health, safety or security, or serious damage to the building
Attend and make safe within 24 hours (follow-on work raised as Urgent or Routine)

Total loss of heating or hot water in winter or where a vulnerable resident lives; uncontrollable leak; dangerous electrics; gas smell (also call the National Gas Emergency line); insecure front door; blocked only toilet; Awaab's Law emergency hazard
A defect that causes significant inconvenience or could get worse quickly
Partial loss of heating; leaking pipe that can be contained; broken window catch where a child lives; electric shower not working (with no other way to wash)
A repair that does not cause an immediate risk or serious inconvenience
Dripping tap; loose kitchen unit; sticking internal door; cracked plaster; gutter overflowing
Larger or non-urgent work that is better grouped or needs specialist planning
Fence renewal; external redecoration; replacing a kitchen unit run; drainage survey
table.caption: Table 2 - Repair priorities

blocks.callout: Any report of damp and mould is triaged under the Damp & Mould Policy and Awaab's Law timescales, not just this table. Advisers must ask the damp screening questions (children, health conditions, extent of mould) on every call that mentions damp, mould, condensation or leaks.
blocks.title: Damp and mould

blocks.p: Where the Keystone tenancy record shows a vulnerability flag, or the resident tells us about a health condition, disability, age over 75 or young children, the adviser should consider raising the priority. For example, a routine heating fault for a resident with a respiratory condition becomes Urgent; a total loss of heating for any resident over 75 between October and April is an Emergency. Careline and SilverLiving residents are always triaged with the scheme coordinator.

bullets: MySilvering app or portal (24/7, with photo upload since April 2026)
Phone the contact centre (8am-6pm weekdays); out of hours, emergencies only via the same number
Email repairs@silvering-homes.org.uk (non-emergency only)
Tell a housing officer, SilverLiving coordinator or an operative during a visit

blocks.p: We offer appointments for all Routine and Urgent repairs: morning (8am-12pm), afternoon (12pm-4pm), school run (9.30am-2.30pm) or first/last of the day. Residents receive a text reminder the day before and when the operative is on the way. If we have to cancel an appointment, we will contact the resident before the slot starts and rebook at their convenience.

Residents must give reasonable access for repairs and safety checks. If we cannot get in at a booked appointment, the operative leaves a calling card and the job returns to the planners' no-access queue. We will try to contact the resident by phone and text within one working day and offer a new appointment. After two failed appointments for a repair, the job is closed and the resident is asked to re-report it - **unless** the repair is a safety issue, a damp and mould case or a statutory check, in which case it is referred to the housing officer and the no-access process in the Compliance Access Procedure applies (warning letters, joint visit, and as a last resort an injunction).

We will recharge residents for repairs caused by deliberate damage, neglect or misuse, for lock changes and lost keys, for clearing items left in empty homes, and for out-of-hours call-outs that turn out to be the resident's responsibility. We will not recharge where damage was caused by domestic abuse, a crime with a crime reference number, or a disability-related reason. Recharges are approved by the Repairs Planning Manager and collected by the Income team; they never affect rent arrears action.

rows: Clearing a blocked toilet caused by misuse
Clearing a void per cubic metre

blocks.p: Secure and assured tenants may claim compensation under our Right to Repair scheme if a qualifying small repair (under £250) is not completed within the prescribed time. Compensation for missed appointments is £20 per appointment, credited to the rent account on request. Wider compensation is considered through the complaints process.

Residents get a text satisfaction survey after each job; results feed the TSM repairs measures (TP02, TP03)
Performance is reported monthly to the Executive Team and quarterly to the Customer Experience Committee

title: Damp and Mould Policy
author: P008
summary: Silvering's zero-tolerance approach to damp and mould, updated for Awaab's Law with the legal timescales for emergency hazards, investigations, written summaries and safety works.

version_history.change: First standalone damp and mould policy following the Housing Ombudsman spotlight report
Dedicated damp surveyor role; 10-day inspection target; follow-up visit at 6 months
Added vulnerability screening questions and dehumidifier loan scheme
Rewritten for Awaab's Law (from 27 Oct 2025): statutory timescales, written summary, alternative accommodation, record keeping. Approved by the Board 22 Oct 2025

blocks.callout: This policy is due for review on 27 October 2026, one year after Awaab's Law came into force. The review is in progress (owner: Director of Property) and this version remains in force until it is replaced.
blocks.title: Review status

blocks.p: Damp and mould can cause serious harm, particularly to children, older people and anyone with a respiratory condition or weakened immune system. {{company.fictional_name}} takes a zero-tolerance approach: we will never blame residents' lifestyles, we will act on every report, and we will fix the cause, not just treat the mould.

This policy covers all homes let on social and affordable rent, older persons and supported housing, and market rent. For shared owners and leaseholders it applies to damp arising from the structure or communal parts we are responsible for. It covers reports from any source: residents, housing officers, operatives, complaints, TSM survey comments, councillors and MPs.

From 27 October 2025 the Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2025 set legal timescales for damp and mould hazards. These are **maximum** timescales; we aim to act sooner wherever we can. Working days exclude weekends and bank holidays.

rows: Emergency hazard (significant risk of harm, e.g. extensive black mould in a baby's bedroom, water through electrics)
Investigate and make safe within 24 hours
Same: surveyor or operative attends within 24 hours; decant considered at the visit
Within 10 working days of becoming aware
Within 10 working days; target 5 working days where a child or vulnerable resident lives
Written summary of findings to the resident
Within 3 working days of the investigation concluding
Within 3 working days, by the resident's preferred contact method
Start safety works for a significant hazard
Within 5 working days of the investigation concluding (or as soon as reasonably practicable where longer works are needed)
Within 5 working days; temporary measures (dehumidifier, mould wash) on the day of the investigation
If the home cannot be made safe within the timescales
Offered at no cost to the resident; Head of Neighbourhoods arranges
table.caption: Table 1 - Awaab's Law and Silvering timescales

numbered: The adviser or officer logs the report in FieldLoop as a damp and mould job and asks the screening questions: Where is the mould? How much? Is anyone in the home under 5, over 75, pregnant, or living with a respiratory, heart or immune condition?
If the answers suggest an emergency hazard, the job is raised as Emergency and the duty surveyor is called directly.
All other reports go to the damp and mould team, who book an investigation within the 10-working-day window. FieldLoop starts the Awaab's Law clock automatically.
Each case is given a case number (DM) and is tracked on the daily breach report.

blocks.p: Investigations are carried out by one of our two damp and mould surveyors. The surveyor will: inspect every room, the loft and the outside of the building; take moisture and humidity readings and photographs; check ventilation, extractor fans, heating and insulation; look at the repairs history for the home and the block; and talk to the household about their health and who lives there. The surveyor assesses the hazard using HHSRS principles and records whether it is a **significant** hazard (Awaab's Law applies) or not significant.

Within 3 working days of the investigation we send the resident a written summary. It must set out: what we found; whether there is a significant hazard; what work we will do and when; the expected timescales; what interim measures are in place; and who to contact. It is written in plain English and is available in other formats and languages on request. A copy is saved in the property's Damp & Mould record on SharePoint and linked in Keystone. The summary is still required where we find no significant hazard - in that case it explains why and what we will do anyway.

bullets: Safety works (e.g. mould treatment, fan installation, leak repair) start within 5 working days of the investigation.
Longer works (e.g. roof, damp-proof course, insulation) are scheduled with a target date in the written summary; interim measures stay in place.
Every case gets a post-works check within 4 weeks and a follow-up visit or call at 6 months.
Cases are closed only when the surveyor confirms the cause is fixed and the resident has been told.

blocks.p: Where a home cannot be made safe within the legal timescales, or the works require it, we will offer suitable alternative accommodation (a decant) at our cost, including removals and reasonable expenses. The resident keeps their tenancy and returns once the home is safe.

We keep a full record of every report, investigation, summary, work order and communication for at least 6 years. A daily breach report goes to the Head of Repairs; monthly performance goes to the Executive Team; quarterly reporting goes to the Customer Experience Committee and the Board.

title: Void Lettable Standard and Void Process
author: P021
summary: The minimum standard every empty home must meet before it is let, and the end-to-end void process from notice to sign-up with targets.

version_history.change: New lettable standard agreed with Resident Panel
Added damp and mould check and EICR on every void
Decoration vouchers increased; major works void definition clarified

blocks.p: An empty home is lost rent and a family waiting. This document sets the standard every home must meet before we let it and the process the voids team, lettings and contractors follow. At 5 November 2026 there were {{fact:voids_current}} homes in the void process; the average void period over the last 12 months was {{fact:void_days_avg_12m}} days and rent loss was {{fact:void_rent_loss_12m}}.
A void is classed as **major works** where it needs a new kitchen or bathroom, rewiring, structural or damp works over £3,000, or asbestos removal.

bullets: New gas safety record (LGSR) and boiler service; gas capped until sign-up and reconnected at sign-up
New EICR (Electrical Installation Condition Report) with any C1/C2 items fixed
Hard-wired, interlinked smoke alarms on every floor and a carbon monoxide alarm next to any fuel-burning appliance
Asbestos survey checked; no works in an area containing asbestos without a refurbishment survey
Damp and mould check by a surveyor with moisture readings; any mould treated and cause fixed
Locks changed on all external doors; three sets of keys
All rubbish, furniture and belongings removed (including loft, shed and garden)
Professionally cleaned, including kitchen, bathroom, windows and floors
All windows open, close and lock; all glazing intact
Kitchen: at least two base units, one wall unit, worktop, sink and space for cooker with a cooker point
Bathroom: working bath or shower, toilet and basin, all with seals renewed
Heating and hot water working in every room
Garden clear and safe; boundary fences in reasonable repair

blocks.p: Walls and ceilings must be sound and free of stains. Where decoration is poor, the new tenant receives a B&Q decoration voucher (£25 per room, maximum £150) instead of a full redecoration. Homes for SilverLiving, supported housing or residents with a disability are fully redecorated.

numbered: **Notice received** (Lettings): pre-void inspection booked within 5 working days; photos and recharges noted; tenant advised on clearing the home.
**Keys returned** (Lettings): void opened in Keystone; utilities and meter readings recorded; Voids Supervisor notified the same day.
**Void inspection** (Voids Supervisor, day 1-2): works order raised in FieldLoop; standard or major works decided; damp check and EICR booked.
**Works** (operatives and contractors): clearance first, then trades in sequence; daily progress in FieldLoop.
**Post-works inspection** (Voids Supervisor): signed off against this standard; any failures fixed within 2 days.
**Ready to let** (Lettings): viewings within 2 working days; sign-up and gas reconnection.

blocks.p: New homes at Orchard Fields are let under the developer handover checklist, not this standard. Defects found at handover are logged with Castlemere Construction through the Development team; the voids team only attends if a defect makes the home unlettable.

title: Repairs Performance Report - October 2026
author: P018
summary: Monthly repairs and damp and mould performance for October 2026, explaining why routine repairs in target fell from May 2026 and the recovery plan.

blocks.p: October was the busiest month for repair reports in two years ({{sql:SELECT reported FROM monthly_repairs WHERE month = '2026-10'}} reported, driven by the first cold snap and Orchard Fields defects being logged as repairs). Emergency performance stayed strong at {{sql:SELECT emergency_pct FROM monthly_repairs WHERE month = '2026-10'}}% in target. Routine repairs remain the problem: {{fact:routine_in_target_oct26}}. The average routine job now takes {{sql:SELECT routine_avg_days FROM monthly_repairs WHERE month = '2026-10'}} days against a 28-day target and {{sql:SELECT routine_avg_days FROM monthly_repairs WHERE month = '2025-10'}} days a year ago.

kv: Brenchley Gardens repairs in target (12 months)
Awaab's Law cases with a timescale breach

table.sql: SELECT month AS Month, reported AS Reported, completed AS Completed, pct_in_target AS "All in target %", emergency_pct AS "Emergency %", urgent_pct AS "Urgent %", routine_pct AS "Routine %", routine_avg_days AS "Routine avg days", first_time_fix_pct AS "First-time fix %" FROM monthly_repairs WHERE month >= '2025-11' ORDER BY month
table.caption: Table 1 - Repairs performance, November 2025 to October 2026 (source: monthly_repairs, FieldLoop)

blocks.h1: 3. Why routine repairs fell from May 2026

blocks.p: Routine performance held between 85% and 92% for 18 months, then fell from {{sql:SELECT routine_pct FROM monthly_repairs WHERE month = '2026-04'}}% in April to {{sql:SELECT routine_pct FROM monthly_repairs WHERE month = '2026-06'}}% in June and has not recovered. Three causes combined:

numbered: **Trade vacancies.** Two electrician posts have been vacant since March 2026 and the plasterer post since May. With only two in-house electricians left, routine electrical work was rationed behind emergencies and EICR remedials. Routine electrical jobs completed in target from May to October fell to {{fact:rep_electrical_routine_6m}}.

**More work sent to Brightline Electrical.** To cover the gap we sent more electrical work to our subcontractor. Brightline's jobs are completed in target only {{fact:rep_brightline_in_target}} of the time, they do not always return job numbers on invoices, and FieldLoop is not updated until the invoice arrives - so jobs look open (and late) for longer than they really are.

**Summer leave.** Leave was not staggered across trades. In August three of the five carpenters and two plumbers were off in the same fortnight, and routine jobs were pushed back to protect emergency and urgent work.

table.sql: SELECT trade AS Trade, COUNT(CASE WHEN completed_date >= '2025-05-01' AND completed_date < '2025-11-01' THEN 1 END) AS "Jobs May-Oct 2025", ROUND(100.0 * AVG(CASE WHEN completed_date >= '2025-05-01' AND completed_date < '2025-11-01' THEN in_target END), 1) AS "In target May-Oct 2025 (%)", COUNT(CASE WHEN completed_date >= '2026-05-01' AND completed_date < '2026-11-01' THEN 1 END) AS "Jobs May-Oct 2026", ROUND(100.0 * AVG(CASE WHEN completed_date >= '2026-05-01' AND completed_date < '2026-11-01' THEN in_target END), 1) AS "In target May-Oct 2026 (%)" FROM repairs WHERE status = 'Completed' AND priority = 'Routine' GROUP BY trade ORDER BY 5
table.caption: Table 2 - Routine repairs completed in target by trade, May-October 2025 vs May-October 2026

blocks.p: Every trade is down, not just electrical, which tells us this is a capacity and scheduling problem across the service rather than a single-trade issue. Damp and mould follow-on works and roofing (Weald Roofing, whose contract ends in December) are also weak.

table.sql: SELECT contractor AS Contractor, COUNT(*) AS Jobs, SUM(status = 'Completed') AS Completed, ROUND(100.0 * AVG(in_target), 1) AS "In target %", ROUND(SUM(cost_gbp), 0) AS "Cost (£)" FROM repairs WHERE contractor IS NOT NULL AND reported_date >= '2026-05-01' GROUP BY contractor ORDER BY Jobs DESC
table.caption: Table 3 - Subcontractor jobs reported since 1 May 2026

blocks.p: Since Awaab's Law came into force we have handled {{fact:damp_cases_awaab}} cases under the regulations. {{fact:damp_breaches}} breached at least one timescale. The most common failure is a late written summary ({{fact:rep_summary_late}} cases), which is an administrative failure we can fix: surveyors are writing summaries at the end of the week rather than the end of each day. {{fact:rep_awaiting_summary_overdue}} open cases are still waiting for a written summary months after the investigation - these are being completed this week.

table.sql: SELECT COALESCE(timescale_breach, 'No breach') AS Outcome, COUNT(*) AS Cases FROM damp_mould_cases WHERE awaabs_law = 1 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY Cases DESC
table.caption: Table 4 - Awaab's Law cases by timescale outcome

actions.action: Recruit two electricians with the market supplement approved by ExCo (adverts live 14 Oct)
Agency plasterer for 12 weeks to clear the plastering and damp follow-on backlog
Brightline to return job numbers on every invoice and update FieldLoop within 48 hours (contract variation)
Saturday overtime blitz on routine jobs older than 28 days at Brenchley Gardens
Leave planning rule: no more than one operative per trade off at the same time from 2027
Surveyors to send written summaries the same day as the investigation

blocks.p: We expect routine performance to recover to 75% by January and 85% by March 2027 if the electrician posts are filled before Christmas.

title: Subcontractor Management Procedure
author: P038
summary: How repairs work is passed to subcontractors, how they are vetted, instructed, monitored and paid, including invoice matching and quality checks.

version_history.change: Added overflow rules for electrical work, FieldLoop update deadline and invoice matching rules after Brightline issues

blocks.p: We use subcontractors for specialist trades and to cover peaks in demand. Residents should not be able to tell the difference: subcontractors work to our Repairs Policy, our timescales and our standards of behaviour. This procedure applies to all repairs and compliance subcontractors listed in the approved supplier list maintained by Procurement.

numbered: Planner raises the job in FieldLoop and assigns it to the subcontractor. A purchase order is created automatically in Northway.
The subcontractor receives the job through the FieldLoop subcontractor portal with the job number, priority, target date and access notes.
The subcontractor must accept the job within 4 working hours (1 hour for emergencies) and book the appointment directly with the resident.
When the job is complete, the subcontractor updates FieldLoop with completion date, notes and photos **within 48 hours**.

blocks.p: While we have electrician vacancies, routine and urgent electrical repairs that cannot be booked in-house within 10 working days are passed to Brightline Electrical. EICR work in occupied homes is passed only with approval of the Compliance Officer.

Invoices must quote the FieldLoop job number and the purchase order number for every line. Invoices without a job number are returned unpaid. The Repairs Planning Manager matches invoices against completed jobs weekly; any invoice line for a job not marked complete in FieldLoop is queried. Variations over £250 need prior approval by a planner.

bullets: Post-inspection of 100% of jobs over £500 and 10% of all others
Monthly KPI return: jobs received, completed in target, first-time fix, recalls, complaints
Quarterly contract meeting with the contract manager; RAG rating reviewed
Two consecutive Red quarters triggers a formal improvement notice

blocks.p: Subcontractor staff must carry Silvering ID, wear overshoes, introduce themselves, and never discuss a resident's affairs. Complaints about subcontractors are handled through our complaints process; the subcontractor must respond to us within 3 working days.

title: Van Stock and Job Sheet Procedure
author: P018
summary: How operatives manage van stock, complete jobs on the FieldLoop app and use paper job sheets when the app is unavailable.

version_history.change: Paper job sheet fallback and 24-hour keying rule; damp observation box added

blocks.p: Fixing a repair on the first visit is better for residents and cheaper for us. Our first-time fix rate over the last 12 months was {{fact:first_time_fix_12m}}. The most common reason for a second visit is that the operative did not have the part on the van.

bullets: Each van carries a standard stock list for the operative's trade (see appendix in FieldLoop)
Operatives scan items used against the job in FieldLoop; stock is replenished from the depot every Tuesday and Friday
Monthly stock check by the Repairs Planning Manager or deputy; variances over £50 investigated
Parts not on the van are ordered through the planners - the job status is set to Awaiting parts with an expected date

numbered: Mark 'on my way' (sends the resident a text)
Arrive, introduce yourself, show ID
Record work done, materials, time on site and photos before/after
Record any further work needed and raise a follow-on job
Record any damp, mould, safety or safeguarding concern (mandatory question)
Ask the resident to sign on the device; mark complete

blocks.p: If the app is not working (no signal in basements, device failure), use a paper job sheet from the van pack. The sheet must record the job number, address, arrival and departure times, work done, materials, further work, any damp or safety observation and the resident's signature.

blocks.callout: Paper job sheets must be handed to the planners and keyed into FieldLoop within 24 hours. Until they are keyed, FieldLoop still shows the job as open and the resident may be chased or sent a survey in error. Scanned sheets are saved in Repairs Procedures/Job Sheets but are image-only and cannot be searched.
blocks.title: 24-hour keying rule

blocks.p: Every operative is a pair of eyes in the home. If you see damp or mould, a gas or electrical danger, signs of hoarding, neglect or abuse, record it and phone the planners before you leave. The planner will raise a damp and mould case (which starts the Awaab's Law clock) or make the right referral.

sql: SELECT d.*, t.postcode, CASE d.hazard_level WHEN 'Emergency' THEN 'an emergency hazard' WHEN 'Significant' THEN 'a significant hazard' ELSE 'not a significant hazard' END AS hazard_text, CASE WHEN d.works_due IS NULL THEN 'No safety works are required because we did not find a significant hazard. We will still carry out the improvement works below as routine repairs.' ELSE 'Because we found a hazard, we must start safety works by ' || strftime('%d/%m/%Y', d.works_due) || '.' END AS works_text, CASE d.cause WHEN 'Condensation (ventilation)' THEN 'Install a humidity-controlled extractor fan in the kitchen and bathroom, check the trickle vents on all windows and treat the affected areas with a fungicidal wash and mould-resistant paint.' WHEN 'Plumbing leak' THEN 'Trace and repair the leak, dry out the affected area with a dehumidifier, then replaster and make good where needed.' WHEN 'Penetrating damp' THEN 'Repair the external defect allowing water in (pointing, render or sealant), then treat and redecorate the affected walls once dry.' WHEN 'Roof or gutter defect' THEN 'Repair the roof covering and clear or replace the guttering, then treat and make good the internal ceiling and walls.' WHEN 'Rising damp' THEN 'Carry out a specialist damp survey and install or repair the damp-proof course, then replaster with a breathable plaster.' ELSE 'Improve insulation at the cold spots identified, treat the mould and fit a humidity-controlled fan.' END AS works_plan FROM damp_mould_cases d JOIN tenancies t USING(tenancy_ref) WHERE d.awaabs_law = 1 AND d.summary_sent_date IS NOT NULL ORDER BY d.reported_date LIMIT 8

blocks.p: Dear {{row.lead_tenant}},

Thank you for letting us know about damp and mould in your home. This letter is your **written summary** of our investigation, which we are required to send you under Awaab's Law. It tells you what we found, what we are going to do, and when.

{{row.surveyor}} visited your home on {{row.investigated_date|date}}. The main cause of the damp and mould is: **{{row.cause}}**. Having assessed the risk to your household's health, we have decided that this is **{{row.hazard_text}}** under the Housing Health and Safety Rating System.
{{row.works_plan}}
{{row.works_text}}

bullets: We can lend you a dehumidifier free of charge - call us to arrange delivery
Keep the doors of rooms with mould closed and use the extractor fans we have provided
Wipe away mould with the kit the surveyor left; do not brush it, as this spreads spores
If anyone in your home becomes unwell, or the mould spreads quickly, call us straight away on our repairs line - we will treat it as an emergency

blocks.p: If you disagree with our findings or we do not keep to these dates, please contact your surveyor first. You can also make a complaint through MySilvering, by phone or in writing, and you can contact the Housing Ombudsman at any time.
Yours sincerely,
**{{row.surveyor}}**, Damp & Mould Surveyor, on behalf of {{company.fictional_name}}
*This summary is available in large print, other languages and audio. Please ask.*

subject: Brightline invoices October - missing job numbers and two recalls
summary: Kwame Asante queries Brightline Electrical's October invoices (no job numbers, jobs still open in FieldLoop) and a quality issue; Brightline responds and Daniel Kerr escalates to a contract meeting.

messages.body:
Hi Darren,

I've been through your October invoices (BEL-10871 to BEL-10889) against FieldLoop and I can't pay most of them as they stand.

1. 14 invoice lines have no FieldLoop job number, only an address and 'electrical works'. Our procedure (and your contract) says every line must have the job number and PO. I've attached the list.

2. At least six of those jobs are still showing as open in FieldLoop because nobody has closed them on the portal. That means they're showing as late in our figures and residents are getting chased by our contact centre for jobs you've done.

3. Two recalls: Flat 16 Parkwood Court (light fitting replaced, failed again after four days) and 64 Catherine Station (socket left without a faceplate - resident has a toddler). Lee found the second one when he was there on a plumbing job.

Can you get me corrected invoices with job numbers and close the jobs on the portal by Wednesday? And please send an engineer back to Catherine Station tomorrow - that one is a safety issue.

Thanks,
Kwame

Morning Kwame,

Apologies - we've had a new admin starting and the job numbers weren't being carried across from the portal into our invoicing system. I'll get corrected invoices to you by Tuesday.

Catherine Station is booked for 11am today, Marcin is going and he'll send you photos.

Parkwood Court - the fitting was the one your stores supplied, so I'm not sure that's on us, but we'll look again at no charge.

On the portal: to be honest our lads find it slow and the login times out. Can we have a call about that? We've doubled the work we do for you since the summer and it's the same two engineers.

Regards,
Darren Wilkes
Contracts Manager, Brightline Electrical Ltd

Dan - FYI below. They've fixed the safety one, but I don't think the job number thing will go away while they're this stretched. He says it's still two engineers, and we've more than doubled what we send them since May.

This is a big part of why our routine electrical figures look so bad. Can we take it to a proper contract meeting rather than me chasing invoices every month?

K

Agreed. Ben - please set up a contract review with Brightline for the week of 9 November. I want on the agenda:

- invoice matching (no job number, no payment - no exceptions from 1 December)
- FieldLoop portal updates within 48 hours, as per the procedure
- capacity: can they actually take what we're sending, or do we need a second overflow contractor
- recalls and post-inspection results

Rob - can you pull their EICR remedial completion rate too, as I want to know whether the compliance work is affected.

Thanks,
Dan

subject: URGENT - damp and mould, 88 Brenchley Gardens (DM1188) - toddler in household
summary: Housing officer Amira Haddad escalates a resident's damp and mould report at 88 Brenchley Gardens after a home visit; the surveyor and Head of Repairs respond on the late investigation and works.

messages.body:
Hi Ellie, Dan,

I visited Sally Newton at 88 Brenchley Gardens today for a tenancy visit. She reported damp on 2 October (DM1188) and nobody has been out yet. She has a two-year-old and the back bedroom - where the little one sleeps - has black mould across the ceiling and behind the wardrobe. The window reveals are wet. I took photos (attached to the Keystone record).

Ms Newton says she was told on the phone to 'keep the windows open and wipe it down'. She's now talking to her councillor.

By my count the 10 working days ran out on Friday 16th. Can someone get out to her this week please? I've told her I'd chase today.

Thanks,
Amira
Housing Officer, Maidstone South

Hi Amira,

Thank you - and sorry. This one was booked for the 15th but Marcus was moved to an emergency at Shepway Green and it didn't get rebooked. That's on us.

I'll go myself tomorrow morning (21st) at 9.30. I'll bring a dehumidifier and a mould kit. If it's as bad as your photos look I'll treat it as significant and we'll get the fan in and mould treatment done inside the 5 days.

I'll send her the written summary the same day.

Ellie

Thanks both.

Ellie - I've seen your notes. Significant hazard, condensation with cold bridging at the balcony slab. Summary went yesterday, which is good. I've asked Kwame to book the fan and the mould treatment for Sunday so we're inside the works deadline of the 28th.

This is recorded as an investigation breach in the breach report. Mark - Ms Newton may well complain; if she does please make sure the stage 1 response acknowledges the missed visit and the advice she was given on the phone. That advice is exactly what the policy says we must never say. I'll raise it with Hannah for the contact centre refresher.

Amira - thank you for pushing this.

Dan

Quick update - Ms Newton says the fan went in yesterday and the room already feels drier. She's still waiting for someone to come back about the wardrobe (it's ruined) and the bedding. Who should I speak to about a goodwill payment?

Amira

title: Repairs - Planners

messages.text: Morning all. Cold weekend = 31 new jobs overnight in the queue, 9 heating. Bradley can you take heating triage first, anyone over 75 or with a vuln flag goes to Urgent minimum.
Two voids at Shepway Green ready for post-inspection today. Can I borrow Kayleigh for snagging this afternoon?
Yes, after her 12-4 at Orchard Fields.

Breach report flagged 3 cases still 'awaiting written summary': DM1160, DM1005 (both Brenchley) and DM1171 Shepway. These were investigated ages ago - Dec, Jan and March. I genuinely think the summaries were written but never logged as sent. Checking the SharePoint folder now.
Not there. They were never sent. I'll write all three today and get them out by email and post.
Thanks Ellie. Please note them on the breach log honestly - don't backdate anything. I'll tell Gareth before the Exec meeting.

Brenchley Saturday blitz 14th and 28th: 14 operatives volunteered so far. I've pulled every routine job at SCH03 older than 28 days - 43 open, 8 overdue. Will group by block so we're not driving round in circles.
Put me down for both. Can someone make sure the overflow kits are on the van this time though, last blitz I lost half a day going back to the depot
Brightline update: Darren says corrected invoices tomorrow. Flat 121 Brenchley (sockets) was assigned to them on the 3rd - nobody has accepted it on the portal yet.
If it's not accepted by midday, bring it back in-house. Justin has a gap Thursday PM.
Agency plasterer confirmed for Mon 9th, 12 weeks. First week all damp follow-on at Brenchley please, there are 7 waiting.

Tablet died at 75 Brenchley this morning, no signal anyway. Paper sheet in the tray. Leak under bath, needs overflow kit + carpenter for the floor. Also black mould in the back bedroom, there is a cot in there for her grandson. She says she reported it in the summer. Can someone raise a DM case?
Thanks Lee. Will key the sheet first thing tomorrow, I'm out at Orchard Fields all afternoon.
@Kwame please don't wait for the sheet to raise the damp case - the Awaab clock starts when we're told, which was 10.12 today. I'll raise it now and go Friday.
Reminder: stand-up 07:45 tomorrow. Bring your no-access lists.

title: Daily repairs stand-up
summary: Daily depot stand-up on 4 November 2026: overnight emergencies, Awaab's Law clocks, Brightline invoices and job acceptance, Brenchley Saturday blitz and agency plasterer.

transcript.text: Right, quarter to, let's go. Quick one today, I've got Exec at ten. Kwame, overnight?

Three emergencies overnight. Burst pipe at 62 Shepway Green, water through the ceiling at 129 Shepway, and a no-heating at Linton Lodge. All made safe, all done by the out-of-hours guys. Dennis did two of them, so he's in late today.
Fine. Who's off?
Justin and Aimee off sick. So we're down one of our two sparks again today, which, yeah.
Which hurts. Okay. Anything Justin had that's a must-do?
Two EICR remedials, I'll ask Rob if Pamela can take them, and the rest I'll push to tomorrow and Friday.
Ellie, clocks.

So. DM1188, 88 Brenchley. Works were due by the 28th, they started the 25th, so that's fine, but it's already logged as an investigation breach because of the missed visit. Ms Newton wants to talk about compensation for the wardrobe.
Send that one to Owen's team as a goodwill request, not a complaint, unless she wants it as a complaint.
Will do. Then DM1084, Flat 47 Brenchley, investigation due Thursday - that's tomorrow - I'm going this afternoon. DM1120 and DM1020 are due the 11th and 12th, both booked for Monday.
Flat 47's the one with the overdue EICR as well, isn't it?
Is it? Oh. I didn't know that.
Yeah, it's on Rob's list. Four no-accesses or something.
Ellie, if you're getting in, can you ring Rob from the doorstep and see if he can get someone round the same day? That's exactly the sort of thing we should be joining up.
Yep. And the three old summaries - they've all gone out now, by email and post, yesterday. I've logged them as late, sent the 3rd.
Good. And from now on?
Same day as the visit. Me and Marcus both. I've made a template on the tablet so we can do it in the van.
Brilliant. Kwame, Brightline.

Fourteen invoice lines with no job number. Darren says corrected invoices today, I'll believe it when I see it. Flat 121 sockets - they never accepted it, so we've brought it back in, Justin Thursday... although Justin's off, so, hmm, I'll look at that.
Ben's setting up the contract meeting for week of the ninth. I want the invoice match done by Friday so I've got the numbers.
By Friday, yes.
Oh and Orchard Fields - six more jobs in, they're all defects really, not repairs. Do I send them to Castlemere?
If it's inside the defects period, yes, through Paul in Development. We're not paying for Castlemere's snagging. Log them, tag them 'defect', send the list to Paul.
Voids - two at Shepway ready for Monday, the Heron Way one's waiting on the EICR. And the agency plasterer starts Monday the ninth.
Put him on the damp follow-ons at Brenchley first week. Lee, anything?
Just the vans. If we're doing the blitz Saturday after next, can we have overflow kits and a few waste traps on every plumber's van? Last time I lost half a day.
I'll do a stock list for the blitz.
Lovely. Saturday blitz numbers, Kwame?
Fourteen volunteers. Forty-three open jobs at Brenchley, eight overdue. I'll group them by block.
Great. That's it. Thanks all. Off you go.
